purpose: Adapters for five strict nineteenth-century microscope-slide nodes where surviving slides can be tied to publication use, named exchange, exact maker labels, or historically bounded teaching/research formation.
guards: A mixed collection that extends after 1899 must be split by dated slide, publication, label, series or creator chronology; do not project later totals into the nineteenth century.
A provenance phrase such as 'sent to X from Y' establishes transfer direction but does not establish that Y prepared or mounted the slide.
A person-lifetime boundary may bound the latest possible transfer date when the source explicitly names the historical sender, but it is not an exact manufacture or exchange date.
A catalogued object or batch is not automatically equal to one glass slide; retain object-count and slide-count namespaces separately unless the museum explicitly states both.
Current surviving totals such as 64 meteorite thin sections or more than 600 Boveri preparations are not nineteenth-century totals when the documented collection spans 1900 or later.
Slides used to document a publication, slides prepared by a named person, and slides merely preserved in that person's foundation are distinct relationships and must remain distinct.

adapters.institution_scope: University of Würzburg Theodor Boveri original Ascaris microscope-slide series
adapters.target: official Würzburg collection/exhibition pages plus the peer-reviewed rediscovery study for the pre-1900 Ascaris slides
adapters.promotion_rule: Use handwritten dates, folder labels, row/section references and publication linkage to isolate the 1894-1898 Ascaris material. Keep the university's more-than-600 surviving Boveri preparations as a whole-collection figure because most counted slides are 1901-1914 sea-urchin work.

adapters.institution_scope: Sorbonne Université Fondation Dejerine histological-slide collection
adapters.target: SorbonNum+ medical collections, SU.MD inventories, official Dupuytren/Dejerine heritage pages and publication-linked case records
adapters.promotion_rule: Isolate pre-1900 slides through SU.MD inventory records and explicit links to nineteenth-century cases/publications, especially the 1895 Anatomie des centres nerveux; do not treat the entire Fondation Dejerine as nineteenth-century because the couple's work continued after 1900.

adapters.institution_scope: Smithsonian NMAH Charles Fasoldt microscope test plate dated April 1884
adapters.target: official NMAH object record MG.M-09770.01, structured identifiers, images and IIIF manifest
adapters.promotion_rule: Preserve the exact maker/place/date wording from the paper label and the NMAH object identifiers. Do not infer the number of glass pieces in the catalogued batch from measurements or object-type wording.

adapters.institution_scope: Harvard MCZ historical Leptogorgia slide sent from Charles Darwin to James D. Dana
adapters.target: official MCZ microscope-slide collection pages and future MCZbase invertebrate item records
adapters.promotion_rule: Keep the source relation exactly as a transfer/provenance claim. The slide is securely nineteenth-century because the explicitly named sender was Darwin, but exact date, preparer and mounting attribution remain unresolved until an item record or correspondence closes them.

adapters.institution_scope: Université de Strasbourg historical meteorite petrographic thin-section collection
adapters.target: official Musée de minéralogie meteorite collection pages, EOST institutional history and surviving thin-section inventory
adapters.promotion_rule: Use Cohen's 1878-1885 Strasbourg tenure, teaching from 1882, supplier labels and any surviving inventory dates to isolate nineteenth-century thin sections. Keep the 64 currently identified slides as a present collection-level total because acquisitions continued around 1900 and later.
